summary: PrivyDrop is a peer-to-peer file transfer utility that uses WebRTC to route text, images, and documents directly between browsers. Because transfers rely on direct browser-to-browser connections rather than central server storage, files move without being permanently cached on an intermediate host. It offers breakpoint-resumable transfers to handle interrupted network connections during transmission.
goodFor: It suits occasional, direct exchanges of large files between trusted parties without relying on third-party cloud storage or email attachments.
watchOut: The codebase has a moderate maintenance tempo and lacks the extensive ecosystem of mature enterprise file-sharing platforms, meaning you may need to troubleshoot issues yourself.
deployNotes: As a containerised Node.js application, it typically requires a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination, though it generally does not need a separate database backend.
